steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Colonel, sorry to keep you waiting for a half hour.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: I'm the one who should apologize, Mr. Vice President. Your schedule in Trimounts is packed, and I heard from Secretary Pavard you had to cancel a meeting on account of my sudden visit.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: The military's response to the District 13 incident has been quick...

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: It has also been intense.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: You had just given such a powerful, rousing speech for the masses. This couldn't have happened at a worse time.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: By the looks of things, this is more than a little 'accident' on your end as well.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: I'm just saying... It's still too soon to reveal the 'Horizon Arc Project' to the public.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Which is why we would like you to cancel the rest of your itinerary and leave Trimounts. And we'll take care of these 'accidents' as soon as we can.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Colonel, I understand what you're asking...

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: But my schedule isn't going to change. In fact, I'm going to extend my stay in Trimounts.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: In my last meeting, I decided I'm going to Rhine Lab to enjoy a fruitful dialogue with our exceptional researchers.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: We're one Columbia, Colonel Blake. We're all ready to give everything for our country.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: But, with all the technological pioneers gathered in this city, they form the bedrock of Columbia's technological development. It's no exaggeration to say they're shaping the future of our country.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Do you understand what I'm getting at?

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Even on the assembly lines of our nation's most developed munitions plants, it takes a day and a half to produce a single shell to spec.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: And that doesn't include the time it takes to send it out into the field to give the men some real practical time on the thing.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Take a step back, Colonel. The more we find ourselves facing superweapons that can change the world, like that 'Arc-01', the more composed we have to be.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: This is Columbia. Not Sargon, not Bolívar.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: These past few years, the Armed Forces, or more accurately, the Department of Defense, has continued to explore the nation's military capabilities.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: As a whole, progress has been fairly steady. From the President's perspective, this is a good thing, and he is glad to see it happen.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: However, given the shifts in international dynamics in recent years, particularly the re-emergence of Victoria's Shard, a number of things have changed.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Such a terrifying superweapon has erased the concept of 'distance.' All our ground defenses will be rendered useless, and the dust brought about by the Storm may well fall upon our pillows at any time.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: The voices within the Department of Defense have grown increasingly hawkish, and a number of troubling signs have already appeared. They're hedging their bets on the research and development of similar era-defining strategic weapons.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: And that's how Kristen caught the military's eye?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Correct. Kristen became the military's core technical advisor.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: In a very short period of time, she submitted the proposal for the 'Horizon Arc Project,' planned the construction of the Arc-01 superweapon, and quickly began its implementation.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: The military has devoted a vast amount of resources to it, and as such, Rhine Lab has enjoyed greater policy-side support for quite some time now.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: This is why Rhine has been able to stand head and shoulders above many other tech companies in Trimounts.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: According to the information we have on hand, the construction of Arc-01 required digging complex S.H.A.F.T.s as well as erecting a H.A.M.H.R.R. at our aircrafts' altitude limit.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: A monumental project indeed, and the military has spared no expense in the effort.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I imagine the man in front of you who fell from the sky was a part of this project.
Saria's eyes shift from the factory ruins to the sky above her.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Using the sky as an intermediary transfer node?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: We don't know the specific conceptual design, or how it's implemented...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Using the sky as a transfer node to focus or redirect an enormous amount of energy, so as to achieve a powerful strike over extreme distance...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: In theory, that is indeed possible...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: But would Kristen really help the military construct a superweapon?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Looks like you didn't get the answer you wanted.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: I knew from the beginning. This just makes it more apparent.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: A good politician would never rush to make his stance clear. At least for now, they don't want us taking over the project that fast.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: And how do they intend to do that?

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: It's simple. All they need to do is delay. If we say that efficiency is the pursuit of scientific research, then, Ferdinand, 'delay' is the preferred tool of these politicians.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: When the Singas administration first entered negotiations in Congress to reclaim the Woods Company's logging camp, virtually no progress was made in three years. It took the latter party losing control of the area.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: They want to delay until we have our hands full, until we lose faith in that damned 'Horizon Arc Project,' until it doesn't matter anymore.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: You've already been on-site, right? What are your conclusions?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: It was indeed the test flight of Arc-01's H.A.M.H.R.R.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: The sky appears clear, but it is far from being a safe haven. Kristen will need to test the new pressure and navigation system, a trial-and-error process that may need more than one flight.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I'm more curious about the military-controlled S.H.A.F.T. at the bottom of Arc-01. Where did Kristen launch a beast of that size?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: The H.A.M.H.R.R.'s black box still hasn't been found? By tracing its routing data, we can triangulate the position of the launch site and locate Kristen.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: We already conducted a full-scale search in District 13. Came up empty.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Someone managed to retrieve the black box at the very beginning.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Any possibility it might've been destroyed, given an explosion of that scope...?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Kristen has already been missing for two weeks. She may have already obtained the experimental data she wanted in the black box, but she still doesn't want us to find her.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: In other words, the so-called 'Horizon Arc Project,' propped up by the military itself, is completely out of the military's hands.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: The longer the delay, the more variables there will be.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: It's me.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: That's right. Jackson had no intention of talking things through with us.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Me? Why would I have anything to hide? Go ask the agent sent to spy on Kristen...

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Understood. I won't give an inch. I'll resolve this situation post-haste.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Wait, what did you say?

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: That's...

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: Alright, I understand.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You don't look so good, Colonel.

steps.name: Blake
steps.text: You're right, Ferdinand. We can't let ourselves get bogged down any longer.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: The fact that Kristen went AWOL while the military had eyes on her precisely shows that the project has progressed to a near-feasible state.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: She might've defrauded her investors.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: We have our suspicious as well, but you seem pretty sure of it, Saria.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Because I know her well enough.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Since its establishment, Rhine Lab has been committed to breakthrough research in civilian technology, and rarely intersects with the military. Kristen herself has no interest in it.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Furthermore...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: If the 'sky' were part of her research plans, it would not be a means, but rather her ultimate objective.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: The Wrights?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Precisely.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: 'We haven't even explored everything these lands have to offer, and have only just begun measuring the heights of the skies. Why fly to such high places in vain?'

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I still remember that comment in the newspaper made by the hovercraft expert, Stevenson, after the Wrights' test flight crashed.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: It encapsulated his regret for the death of the genius scientists, but has been twisted out of context as 'accurate peer review.' How ironic that it's become a weapon used against the Wrights.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I'd like to hear more.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Stevenson had a very good relationship with the Wrights, and even looked after Kristen to some degree after their passing. Later, Kristen was able to get on track in academia thanks to his recommendation.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: A substantial secret that even I'm not aware of.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: But, the relationship between Stevenson and Kristen is not a cozy one. She inherited her parents' obsession with the skies, and does not expect others to understand.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: She abhors the sky, Tin Man.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It can't be a coincidence that Transmitter appeared at the scene of the accident, but what exactly is the connection between Transmitter and the explosion?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Did the things used in this factory require Transmitters? I recall no such relationships between Triton Chemicals and Rhine Lab. Or, perhaps, the Transmitter had something to do with the ring-shaped mechanical object that smashed through the factory building...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Saria's too far away. I can't hear what she's saying...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Maybe I can try moving the drone a bit closer.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: An unidentified drone has been shot down.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Oh no...

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Miss, show me your security clearance.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Don't have one? District 13 is under temporary lockdown. I'm gonna have to ask you to come with me.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm a worker at the Triton factory. I had the day off today, but I heard the factory exploded... so I came here to see what's going on.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: If you're a worker at the factory, then explain the drone. And don't say you have nothing to do with it.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I—
She's going to photograph the site.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Marianne...?!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Is it really you? Oh my g—

steps.name: Marianne
steps.text: Marianne...

steps.name: Marianne
steps.text: The last time I heard that name... was forty years.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: You're talking about that press conference, right? It was right around the time your last movie came out, you told the world you got hurt in a Catastrophe while shooting the thing, and you retired to behind-the-scenes work...

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: My dad goes nuts every time he talks about you!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: He's got your complete filmography collection, and we've watched every movie ten times over!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: I still remember 'The Spy Catchers'! You caught saw the spy on the shore and leapt straight off that cruise ship! That was something...

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: You just melt into every role you play. Today's mass-produced Wrankwood stars could take a cue or two from you.

steps.name: Marianne
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Marianne
steps.text: Unfortunately, the only role Marianne plays these days is a negotiator of employee salaries.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: You're...

steps.name: Marianne
steps.text: Director of Human Resources at Rhine Lab, Jara Booker Wilson. This is my clearance. I have a house in District 13.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: This woman is indeed a Triton employee. Rhine Lab and Triton Chemicals had a number of... disagreements. Just like the corporate struggles in 'The Spy Catcher'...

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: I know. This is Trimounts, after all.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: A subsidiary factory suddenly went up in flames. If photos from the scene hit the tabloids, that would send Triton down in scandal. This is her housewarming gift for joining Rhine.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: That would indeed be a violation of military regulations. Fortunately, the drone's been shot down, so the photos won't leak.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Now then, let's move on and discuss your job-hopping.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...Sure.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: But let me add something first. Isn't it a little unreasonable to suddenly ask the locals to lock themselves inside and wait for updates before they can do anything?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: We're just following orders.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Miss Marianne, I... I want to trust you. So, both of you, please leave. No exceptions.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Your name's Silence, right? I remember you were helping Parvis bring me some black bean tea.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Director Jara, does this have something to do with Rhine Lab?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: That's why you snuck in here?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: There are... some things I need to make sure of.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: This isn't exactly the best place for chit-chat.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Head over here, and wait for me.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Where are we...?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Don't worry. It's my District 13 residence.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: I have company. An old friend has some business with me.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: I don't think I've ever heard you breathing. When you smoke, are you just letting it swirl around your stomach?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: It's a habit. Just like what you used to do after finishing a mission. You'd record the event on a note before burning it on the spot.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: That young researcher back there... You always have a soft spot for the youth.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Eh, can't exactly ignore it, can I?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: An employee of my own company shows up in a military lockdown, it'll be bad for business if she gets caught.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I see you're just as attentive to detail as ever, regardless of what field you're in.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: You've caught my eye a number of times over the years. From the intermediary investor for all of Trimounts to the head of Rhine HR, you've contributed pretty much your entire network to this tech company.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: In other words, without you, we wouldn't have the Kristen we know today.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: So, is you being here right now also the fault of that reckless girl?

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Or, do you have ideas of your own?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Have you considered the possibility that I'm here because I bought a residence in District 13, and that I spend a few days here when I'm not too busy?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: I'm getting old, Tin Man.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Age notwithstanding, when I came back to my senses, I realized that my health, my dreams, my friends, and my family... had all been given to my country.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: In the end, nothing remained of Maylander's 'Morningstar.'

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: I don't even have any tapes of the movies I made when I was young by which to remember my so-called 'youth.'

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: I wasn't trying to point the finger at you, Jara.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: But if you're hoping that I turn a blind eye to this, I'm afraid I can't help you... Maylander's only responsibility is to the country.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: I just wanted to tell you I have no regrets. So even now, I won't do anything that would truly harm Columbia.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Are you still mourning the death of the Wrights?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: As much as I'd like to deny it, the scene still haunts my dreams even now.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Delivery. Come sign for it.
Put it on the workstation.
Ho'olheyak scans the space in front of her, a massive, hollow underground ring-shaped structure. In other words, a 'well.'

Originium lamps fastened to the well's walls provided only a basic lighting, making it difficult to determine the overall depth. Inlaid within the grooves running along the walls are cables extending into the darkness.
The person with who she was speaking earlier is now pacing back and forth, leaving her with but a busy silhouette.

She seems to be busy testing something. Even in such a deep area, her actions do not seem to cause much of an echo. Presumably, the surface structure incorporates some high-performance sound-absorbing material.
The entire area seems to be as still and silent as lingering mist.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Are you not afraid of the dark? Do you not get bored? We're several hundred meters underground... and those boorish soldiers are patrolling just above us.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: You've been here a number of months, right? Haven't gone up for a walk?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Nasti?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I'm busy, K'uk'ulkan.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: I don't have much free time on my hands, either.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: What I'm saying is, put the black box down, and get lost.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: I'm taking a risk here to get this to you under the watchful eyes of the military and Maylander. That's a bit cold of you, wouldn't you agree?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: This is a deal between you and Control. It's got nothing to do with me.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You didn't do anything with the black box after you got your hands on it, did you?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Damn, ice cold.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: The data calculations are... Well, not that complicated.
Nasti dives back into her own work, and the screen is once again engulfed with a large amount of data, like a tide flooding across land.
She focuses up more, leaving Ho'olheyak alone to do little else than stare at her back. That is when she notices the devices around her waist–
They appear as a lattice of dead branches, spliced together irregularly. But as Nasti intermittently works at her station, they sway back and forth in a short, regular rhythm.
As if sentient, they seem to be following Nasti's thoughts.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Looks like you managed to find nourishment for the rootless branches... Hmph.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: The trajectory data has deviated slightly from the previous calculation, but is still within the expected range. It appears that Transmitter can indeed be used as an alternative navigation resource.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: That being the case, we need to speed things up.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: By the way, how did Kristen get you, the head of Engineering, to willingly coop yourself up underground to do the hard work for her?

Nasti doesn't answer. She enters a few commands, and as the screens in front of her go dark one by one, she turns and heads towards the door. Behind her, the underground space becomes dimmer and dimmer.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Ready to touch some grass, Nasti? Did something good happen? Surely you're not going to keep the good news from me?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) Begone.
Ho'olheyak takes a step back upon hearing that one word. Her body instinctively carries out the order, as if executing a 'command.'

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Cute curse you have there, Banshee.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Did any of the staff ever tell you you've got a bad temper?
The icy-cold air caresses Nasti's neck before dissipating like an illusion. The young banshee shivers slightly.
A crack forms across the bone pen in her hand.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Oh my, they don't quite make them like they used to, do they? I know you have an entire drawer filled with spares.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: But, I've always been curious... if you broke all of your bone pens, would you still be able to perform your little tricks?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Go ahead and try me.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I won't give the same command twice, K'uk'ulkan.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Fine, fine. Are all Banshees as much of a stick in the mud as you?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Don't pass up on this rare opportunity to get some fresh air. If you're afraid of the dark, I don't mind keeping you company partway.
Before the banshee can speak again, Ho'olheyak nimbly disappears behind the door.
The darkness lingering within the air trembles violently for a spell, then Nasti finally lets go of her words.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: ...Ugh.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I should go pick her up.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) At last, the muddled dream is about to settle.
